skill.name: file-organizer
skill.description: Organizes local files and folders by reviewing directory contents, finding duplicates, proposing cleaner structures, and applying approved cleanup actions.
skill.summary: Plan and apply safer folder cleanup workflows with user approval.
skill.author: ComposioHQ

security_audit.summary: All static external-command and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline paths, and ordinary file naming guidance. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md. The remaining security concern is the intended cleanup workflow, which can move or delete local files after user approval.

remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit target directory, show a dry-run plan, and record every move or rename before applying changes.

remediation.issue: Duplicate deletion can remove wanted files
remediation.suggestion: Confirm duplicates with hashes, keep backups or archives first, and require separate confirmation for each deletion group.
Tell users when commands differ by operating system, quote paths safely, and prefer read-only commands during analysis.

content.user_title: Organize Files and Clean Up Folders
content.value_statement: Messy folders make files harder to find and increase duplicate storage. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code analyze folders, plan cleanup, and apply approved changes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews directory listings, file types, sizes, and file age using local shell commands.
Groups files by type, purpose, date, or project context.
Finds duplicate candidates by hash, filename, and size.
Proposes folder structures and move plans before changes.
Creates folders and moves or renames files after approval.
Produces cleanup summaries and maintenance tips.
limitations: Requires the user to choose the target directory and approve changes.
Duplicate detection examples may need operating system adjustments.
Ambiguous file names may require user decisions.
Approved moves or deletions can still cause data loss.

use_cases.title: Clean a Downloads Folder
use_cases.description: Sort documents, images, installers, archives, and unclear files into a cleaner structure.

use_cases.title: Prepare Project Archives
use_cases.description: Separate active projects from old work and create an archive layout for long-term storage.

use_cases.title: Reduce Duplicate Files
use_cases.description: Find duplicate candidates, compare metadata, and decide which copies should stay.

prompt_templates.title: Clean One Folder
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup for a single messy folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me organize my Downloads folder. First analyze what is inside, then suggest folders and ask before moving anything.

prompt_templates.title: Find Duplicate Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Find duplicate files in my Documents folder. Show likely duplicate groups, recommend which copies to keep, and ask before deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure Projects
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Projects folder. Separate active, archived, learning, and template projects. Provide a dry-run plan before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Cross-Folder Archive
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced archive planning across multiple locations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a conservative archive plan for Documents, Desktop, and Downloads. Avoid current projects and require confirmation for every move.

output_examples.input: Organize my Downloads folder with many documents, images, and installers.
output_examples.output: A summary of file counts, proposed folders, files needing decisions, and a confirmation request before moving anything.

output_examples.input: Find duplicate proposal files in Documents.
output_examples.output: A grouped duplicate review with file paths, sizes, dates, a recommended copy to keep, and a deletion confirmation prompt.

output_examples.input: Review my Projects directory and suggest improvements.
output_examples.output: A project structure audit, an active versus archive split, naming recommendations, and a step-by-step cleanup plan.

best_practices: Start with one folder and review the plan before approving changes.
Keep an archive or backup before deleting duplicate files.
Use clear naming rules that match how you search for files.
anti_patterns: Do not organize an entire home folder without a narrow scope.
Do not delete duplicates based only on matching names.
Do not move active project files without checking dependencies.

faq.question: Does this skill move files automatically?
faq.answer: It is designed to propose a plan first and ask for approval before moving or deleting files.

faq.question: Can it find duplicate files?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests hash, name, and size checks to identify duplicate candidates.

faq.question: Will it work on every operating system?
faq.answer: The workflow is general, but some shell commands need changes for macOS, Linux, or Windows.

faq.question: Can it organize photos by date?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose year and month folders using metadata or file modification dates.

faq.question: Is it safe for important work files?
faq.answer: Use a narrow target folder, review the dry-run plan, and keep a backup before approving changes.

faq.question: Can it create a long-term archive?
faq.answer: Yes. It can separate active files from archived files and suggest a maintainable folder structure.
